title: Tom return-to-value with near-band placebo (|d|<=1) as primary, fresh pre-DEV data BTCUSDT 2020-2021

what.name: Source
what.value_plain: Tom Vorwald 70/30 return-to-value claim (extract_BB3c8visnkI.md:38); test from SETUP_REVIEW sec 6 test 2
what.label: SOURCED

what.name: Event and outcome
what.value_plain: first 5m close outside prior UTC-day value area (bin 10 USD, VA 70%); RETURN = a later 5m bar that touches the prior POC
what.label: OURS

what.name: Placebo
what.value_plain: same levels shifted by d x ATR14(1h), primary restricted to |d|<=1 (d in -1,-0.5,0.5,1)
what.label: OURS

what.name: Costs
what.value_plain: none: a count of a claim, no trade
what.label: OURS

how: Count of return shares, real band vs shifted band on the same kind of days; 95% day-block bootstrap (2000 resamples) of the difference. Pre-registered before the run.
window: DEV_EXT 2020-01-02 to 2021-12-31 (before DEV); DEV, VALIDATION and HOLDOUT not read

verdict.label: FAIL: real minus near-band placebo +4.4 pp, CI -0.3..8.9 includes 0

why: Real prior-day value returns to POC 63.4% of event days vs 58.9% for a band shifted by at most one ATR; the CI of the gap spans zero (n 352 / 353).
The large pooled gap (+12.9 pp) comes from far-shifted bands (|d|>=2), which are unlike value for any reason; a band near value behaves like value.
Fewer events than the card's ~870 (352 vs ~870) because |d|<=1 keeps half the days and perp 1m data starts 2020-01; a true +4 pp gap is not excluded.
